title: Grateful Dead Live at Reno Centennial Coliseum on 1982-03-13
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Apogee Ensemble -> Peak -> AIFF  Mastering Info: AIFF -> Samplitude Professional v11.2 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Clean soundboard capture of a high‑energy second set featuring a smoking Stranger > Franklin’s and a soaring The Other One
ai_review.review: The recording is a pristine soundboard source that delivers crystal‑clear separation and a very clean mix, letting the band’s interplay shine. Musically the show is a standout second‑set highlight reel – Stranger into Franklin’s rolls into Space and an enthusiastic Other One, with memorable moments like Jerry’s slipknot tease at the end of Eyes. Overall the performance feels loose yet inspired, characteristic of the early‑’82 era.

ai_rating.rationale: Reviews overwhelmingly praise both the musical energy (many 4–5 star comments) and the clean soundboard recording; only one low‑star outlier exists, so the combined weighted rating is strong.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Very clean board mix with distinct instrument separation; no reported dropouts or muddiness.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Second set flows tightly from Stranger into Franklin's, launches into a cosmic Space segment and then builds into an enthusiastic The Other One; transitions are praised as seamless.

band_member_comments.Jerry: False start on He's Gone before settling into Eyes; notable slipknot tease at the end of Eyes; great guitar/Weir exchange during Stranger.
band_member_comments.Phil: Dropping bombs on bass noted, especially in the spring‑summer ’82 style.
band_member_comments.Bob: Strong rhythm and vocal presence highlighted through the Weir/Jerry exchange on Stranger.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent Mydland’s electric piano is praised as fully integrated, adding depth to the jams.
